sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the eighth day of Chanukah has two interpretations, but the primary focus is on the drawing down into Malchus below.

translations.translation: And seemingly it must be said,
that this is the case regarding the eighth day of Chanukah,
that it has two interpretations.
For that which on the eighth day the drawing down is into Malchus
(therefore it is called Chanukah),
the eighth that is below the seven,
is because its root is in the eighth that is above the seven.
But from that which in the aforementioned maamar
(which explains the concept of the eighth day of Chanukah)
is brought
(at the beginning of the topic16)
only the interpretation that the eighth is Malchus,
and not as in the discourses that explain the concept of the eight days of the inauguration in which both interpretations of the eighth are brought,
it implies,
that the primary concept of the eighth day of Chanukah is the drawing down below.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section uses analogies of a lever and a house to explain how elevating the lowest power (action) elevates all higher powers completely.

translations.translation: And this will be understood based on what is known,
that regarding the superiority of action
[for the power of action in man,
the lowest power,
is analogous to the Sefirah of Malchus]
there are several concepts.
This, that specifically through action an elevation is made in all the powers of the soul.
And as is known the parable for this from the lifting tool called a lever,
that by placing it under the entire thing one wishes to lift,
then specifically the entire thing is lifted.
For when one lifts the thing from its middle,
then its lower part remains below.
And like the lifting of a house,
that in order for the entire house to be lifted upward it is specifically by lifting the lowest beam of the house,
and when one lifts the walls from their middle,
the lower beams remain below17.
And it can be said,
that since all the beams are of one house,
therefore,
when the lowest beam remains below,
also the lifting and elevation of the upper beams is not complete.
And all the more so in the analogue of the powers of the soul,
that each power influences the other powers18,
that in order for the elevation of the higher powers
(intellect etc.)
to be complete,
it is specifically through the elevation of the power of action,
the lowest power.
And another concept in this,
that through action,
the elevation and lifting of the higher powers is to a higher place.
And like the analogy of the scale pan in which one weighs on one pan and places a weight on the second pan,
that the more the pan in which one weighs descends downward,
the lifting of the weight in the second pan is higher upward19.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the root of action is above all other powers, both in that it draws from the essence of the soul and in that its own root is in the soul's essence.

translations.translation: And behold, that specifically through action the complete elevation of all the powers is achieved is because the root of action is above all the powers.
And there are two concepts in this20.
That the drawing down into action
(that intellect and emotions are drawn into action),
its root is in the soul that is above the powers.
For intellect and emotions in themselves are limited and it is not within their ability to descend so low and become clothed in action,
and that it is possible for them to descend and become clothed in action is because there is drawn into them from the soul,
which exists in all the powers and limbs equally.
And that the root of the power of action itself is above the root of all the powers.
For that all the powers are in the category of closeness to the soul and the power of action is a separate power,
is because the root of all the powers is in the revelations of the soul,
and the root of the power of action is in the essence of the soul21.
